newsitem.title: USA: U.S. envoy Ross to return to Middle East.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy Ross to return to Middle East.

text.p: The United States, concerned at "the recent drift" in the Middle East peace process, is sending special envoy Dennis Ross back to the region at the weekend, Secretary of State Warren Christopher said on Thursday.
Christopher told a year-end news conference the risk of fresh acts of terrorism in the Middle East made it essential to "regain and restore momentum" in the peace process.
"The president and I have been concerned about the recent drift in the peace process," Christopher said. "To re-energise this effort we are sending Dennis Ross to the region this weekend."

Christopher said Ross, the State Department's special Middle East coordinator, would report on the status of Israeli-Palestinian negotiations and would return before Christmas "so that we can have an up-to-date assessment."

Both Christopher and President Bill Clinton have voiced frustration this week with the slow pace of negotiations over the pullout of Israeli troops from the West Bank town of Hebron and over Israel's policy on settlements in the West Bank.

Israel and the Palestinian Authority renewed talks on Monday. Hebron is the last of seven West Bank towns from which Israeli troops are supposed to redeploy under previous accords, but the talks are bogged down over security arrangements for Hebron's 400 Jews.
Ross attended the first three weeks of the Hebron talks in October as a mediator, but has not been back since. Christopher gave no indication he would step into the negotiations again now.

"The Israelis have made some moves in connection with Hebron. We think it's time for the Palestinians, for chairman (Yasser) Arafat to respond to those moves, to reciprocate those moves," Christopher said.
The secretary of state said his main fear was the resumption of acts of terrorism in the region, and implicitly called on Arafat to prevent any attack by Arab guerrillas.

"There are still people who are obviously hostile to the peace process and that's one of the reasons why we need to try to regain and restore momentum in the peace process because of the risk in a hiatus of some kind of a terrorist incident," he said.
"I strongly urge President Arafat and all those who are involved to take every action that they can to ensure that there's no recurrence of violence," he said.
